title: Tunnels
searchPlaceholder: Search name, public endpoint or target

httpApi.name: HTTP + WebSocket API
httpApi.detail: Gateway mode, shares 443, routed by Host

delete.title: Delete tunnel {{slug}}
delete.warn: The entry listener closes immediately and in-flight sessions are cut.

target.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; it shows up in URLs and logs
target.withAgentHint: Run the agent on the target's machine; the final say over the target address stays with the agent
target.withoutAgentHint: v1 has no relay-side dial path — all three data-plane entries require a live agent. A tunnel created this way stays at "waiting for agent", or gets bound to whichever agent happens to be online (the opposite of this choice). It is unimplemented because the relay would first need the same target policy the agent enforces; without it that path has no SSRF defence.
target.addrHint: The agent re-checks the resolved address on every dial; cloud metadata addresses are permanently denied

protocol.udpHint: UDP rides unreliable datagrams, one-to-one with UDP semantics; one stalled flow never blocks the others
protocol.sharedUdpDisabled: UDP carries neither SNI nor a Host header, so shared-port routing only makes sense for TCP.
protocol.routerAuto: Derived from the mode: gateway → by Host and path, passthrough → by SNI (SNI is cleartext, reading it needs no decryption).
protocol.listenPortHint: Leave empty to let the relay allocate
protocol.hostRewriteHint: Required for nomifun-tauri targets: its host guard 403s any domain-shaped Host

mode.question: How should the relay handle TLS?
mode.passthroughTagline: The relay only moves ciphertext; it never decrypts
mode.gatewayTagline: The relay terminates TLS and routes by Host / path
mode.passthroughPro1: Private key stays on your server
mode.passthroughPro2: End-to-end encryption; zero trust in the relay
mode.passthroughCon1: No ACME — certificates are your problem
mode.passthroughCon3: No HTTP-layer metrics (status codes / paths / per-request latency)
mode.passthroughCon4: Backend cannot see the real client IP; only PROXY protocol can restore it
mode.gatewayPro3: Can inject auth / XFF real IP
mode.gatewayPro4: Status code / path / per-request latency metrics
mode.gatewayCon1: Private key and plaintext pass through the relay
mode.gatewayCon2: Still works for ESP32 without SNI (cleartext http/ws)
mode.disabledHostRewrite: This template must rewrite the Host header, which passthrough cannot do by definition — it never reads plaintext. Hence unavailable.

compare.hostRouting: Host / path routing, many tunnels on 443
compare.realIP: Backend sees the real client IP
compare.esp32: ESP32 on a bare IP, no SNI

gatewayOnly.reason: In passthrough the relay never decrypts, so this field has no effect. Switch to gateway to enable it.

exposureStep.title: Exposure surface
exposureStep.note: When a device can only take an IP + port, the boundary can only live at the network layer. Once traffic flows, Learn mode can pin the observed sources into an allow-list in one click.
exposureStep.confirmOpen: This tunnel is open to any address with no app-layer auth, so confirmation by name is required.
exposureStep.ppsHint: Must accompany the byte limit: 100k pps of 64-byte packets is a real attack that a bytes-only limiter waves through

preview.title: Generated config preview
preview.hint: The console teaches, the file commits. The relay never reads console edits back out of the file.

probe.title: Per-hop probe
probe.fromInternetHint: Loopback will lie to you: reachable locally is not reachable publicly
probe.okPartial: Every hop we could measure passed, but {{count}} hop(s) were not tested (marked "—" above) — this does not mean end-to-end works
